t: You're at the site of Queen Alexandra's Military Hospital, just north of Tate Britain beside the Thames, on the edge of Millbank and Pimlico. It opened in July 1905 and closed in 1977, though several of the buildings remain. It takes its name from Alexandra of Denmark, who was Queen from 1901 to 1910 as the wife of Edward VII. Several senior officers died here, including Admiral of the Fleet Sir Charles Forbes, who commanded the Home Fleet in 1940, and General Sir Cecil Sugden, who was Master-General of the Ordnance in the last year of his life.
